cost: Knapsack value scaling O(n^3/epsilon); trimmed subset list O(n*L*log L), L=O(n*log(target)/epsilon) in the mathematical model. Interpolation validates O(n) then searches O(log n); dot O(n). Work and allocation limits apply.
description: Compute bounded-loss feasible objectives, exact rational interpolation and quantized integer dot observations with distinct certificates.
forward: Compute bounded-loss feasible objectives, exact rational interpolation and quantized integer dot observations with distinct certificates.

Embedding subset values as equal knapsack weights/profits preserves the exact optimum. The two approximate outputs may differ while satisfying their own loss bounds. Conditional absolute interpolation error transports through a known Lipschitz map; dot L1 normalization does not imply relative scalar error under cancellation.
inverse: Exclude infeasible or over-optimal FPTAS outputs, violated declared loss bounds, extrapolated interpolation, and true dot errors outside the absolute certificate. Exclude promotion of caller curvature to checked fact and promotion of L1-normalized dot error to cancellation-relative error.

Objective certificates admit many item lists and optimal subsets. One interpolated ordinate admits many functions through the supplied knots; dot values admit sign/permutation and cancellation fibers. Reconstruct only constraints retained by the certificate, not unique original inputs.
limitations: Curvature bound is a caller premise, not inferred from knots. Overflow, work limits and allocation failures do not count as small approximation errors. Integer certificates do not provide a shared parent percentage or universal speed gain.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
state: Feasibility, objective loss, conditional interpolation error and dot absolute/L1 error remain separately typed. Unsupported percentages and resource/arithmetic errors are categorical.
